node.title: Quotient-periodic pencils survive the twenty-fiber SPI interface
node.closure: explicit power-map pencils show that the bounded exception-SPI hypotheses alone do not cap the number of split fibers
node.statement: Let the smooth domain be the cyclic group mu_N with N a power of two. For every e in {1,2,4,8} dividing N and every y in mu_{N/e}, the monic polynomial X^e-y has exactly e roots in mu_N; these roots form one coset of mu_e. Distinct y give disjoint fibers. Taking u=X^e, v=1 and slope gamma=-y therefore yields N/e pairwise-disjoint split squarefree degree-e fibers of the pencil u+gamma v, with gcd(u,v)=1 and nonzero constant locator scalar. On the official N=2097152 domain, N/e is at least 262144, far above twenty. Thus the exact degree-1-through-11, twenty-disjoint-fiber SPI interface does not by itself imply emptiness or a bounded fiber count. A closing theorem must identify and price quotient-periodic power-map classes or use additional received-line, factor-owner, denominator, or chronology semantics. This is an algebraic route fence, not an MCA counterexample.
